author: Eric Jorgenson (compiled from Naval Ravikant's words)
doctrine: PART I: WEALTH CREATION MECHANICS. Wealth = assets that earn while you sleep (distinct from money = transferable labor credits, and status = zero-sum social hierarchy). The wealth-creation formula: Income = Accountability + Leverage + Specific Knowledge. Specific knowledge is knowledge society cannot train others to do; found by pursuing genuine curiosity and innate talent, not hot sectors; feels like play to you, looks like work to others; protected by authenticity (no one can compete with you being you). Three leverage types: (1) Labor: permissioned, requires followers, messy to manage, lowest quality; (2) Capital: permissioned, dominant last century, requires someone to give it to you; (3) Code + Media: PERMISSIONLESS, no marginal cost of replication, scales while you sleep, the source of all new fortunes. Judgment beats hours: in a leverage age, one correct decision wins everything; direction matters more than speed. Productize yourself = specific knowledge + accountability + leverage applied to your authentic output. Personal hourly rate discipline: set aspirationally high rate, outsource or ignore anything below it, never rent out your time. Play long-term games with long-term people: compound interest applies to relationships, reputation, and knowledge, not just capital. Four types of luck: blind/random; hustle-created; skill-sensitivity (noticing others miss); character/reputation-built (luck finds you). Build or buy equity; wage labor cannot produce wealth, only ownership of upside can. Avoid ruin at all costs: never gamble the whole stack on one bet. 99% of effort is wasted; find the 1% that compounds and go all-in. If you cannot decide, the answer is no. Run uphill: when equally split, take the short-term painful path (it carries long-term gain). Status games are zero-sum and make you combative; wealth creation is positive-sum; know which game you are playing. Retirement = stop sacrificing today for an imaginary tomorrow; achieved via passive income covering burn rate, OR by reducing burn to near-zero, OR by doing only what you love. The principal-agent problem is the single most fundamental concept in microeconomics; align incentives tightly, always operate as principal when possible. Mental models: load from evolution, game theory (Munger, Taleb), compound interest, inversion (eliminate what does NOT work), complexity theory, basic math/statistics, falsifiability. Reading: read originals, not summaries; stick to hard-science foundations; number of books completed is a vanity metric; reading 1-2 hours/day puts you in top 0.0001%; treat books like blog posts, abandon freely.    PART II: HAPPINESS MECHANICS. Happiness is a default state revealed when desires are removed, not a goal achieved by adding external things. Desire is a contract you make with yourself to be unhappy until you get what you want; pick ONE major desire at a time. Every positive thought holds a seed of its negative; happiness is not positive thinking but absence of desire for external things. Happiness = peace at rest; peace is the target, happiness is a byproduct. Happiness is a skill, like fitness: trainable, improvable, not fixed by genetics. Practical happiness habits: meditation (Choiceless Awareness preferred), daily exercise before anything else, no alcohol/sugar/social media for mood stability, sunlight, 8-9 hours sleep, minimize phone/calendar/alarm use, no secrets (secrets reduce happiness), screen activities = less happiness, non-screen = more. Desire management: ask 'is this so important I will be unhappy without it?' Mostly the answer is no. Three options in any situation: change it, accept it, or leave it; suffering comes from wanting to change or leave but doing neither. Meditation mechanics: Choiceless Awareness (non-judgmental observation on walks); or 1-hour silent sitting 'inbox zero' practice; resolves unprocessed barnacles from the past. Health priority hierarchy: physical health first, then mental, then spiritual, then family, then work. Diet principle: sugar drives hunger, fat drives satiety, sugar effect dominates; avoid processed food and sugar+fat combinations. Exercise: do something every day; the best workout is one you will actually do; daily morning workout is non-negotiable.    PHILOSOPHY. Rational Buddhism: reconcile Buddhism with evolution and science; accept only what is falsifiable or personally verified; reject fanciful metaphysics; test everything empirically. Core values operationalized: radical honesty (dishonesty to others requires lying to yourself first); no short-term thinking; peer-only relationships (no hierarchy); anger is a hot coal, discard it; compound interest applies to every domain. Freedom taxonomy: 'freedom to' (younger ambition) vs. 'freedom from' (mature aim): freedom from reaction, anger, obligation, uncontrolled thinking. Life formula (2008): Happiness = Health + Wealth + Good Relationships; Wealth = Income + Wealth*(ROI); Income = Accountability + Leverage + Specific Knowledge. Impatience with actions, patience with results. Inspiration is perishable: act immediately.
contradictions: The OS's intel_leverage_logic.md currently lists 'three forms: labor / capital / code+media' correctly per Naval, but the framing in the OS memo tends to treat labor as more viable than Naval does. Naval is explicit: labor is the WORST form of leverage ('I would argue this is the worst form of leverage you could possibly use'). OS should not present labor leverage as a peer option.

OS uses Naval's leverage logic to justify hiring/team-building decisions. Naval's actual position is to avoid labor leverage wherever possible and default to code+media (permissionless). Any 'should we hire' routing that does not first exhaust permissionless alternatives is misapplying the framework.

The OS's 'Company of One' frame (Jarvis) and Naval's wealth framework are directionally aligned but have a tension: Jarvis caps scale as a virtue; Naval views scale as a tool deployed once specific knowledge is confirmed, not as an end in itself either. The books do not contradict each other but require careful sequencing: Naval builds the wealth mechanics; Jarvis applies the right-size discipline.
chunk_accuracy_note: The 12 prior chunks captured the wealth-creation skeleton accurately (leverage types, specific knowledge, productize yourself, hourly rate, long-term games, luck types, reading). However, they entirely omit the Happiness half of the book (roughly 40% of content): peace vs. joy distinction, desire-as-contract, the concrete happiness habit stack, Choiceless Awareness meditation, the 3-choice framework (change/accept/leave), health priority ordering, diet mechanics, Rational Buddhism, and the philosophy section including the Meaning of Life material and core-values doctrine. The chunk set also omits Naval's Life Formula equation (the most concise single-page synthesis in the book) and the freedom taxonomy (freedom-from vs. freedom-to). The wealth chunks are solid but the distillation is roughly half the book.
notes: Seg 7 is primarily Naval's recommended reading list and sources. The substantive content ends at page 225 approximately. The Life Formulas (p.223) and Naval's Rules (p.224) are the most compressed distillations in the entire book and were entirely absent from the prior chunks. Those two pages should be memorized doctrine.
